content.title: Reading experience and proficiency as predictors of relative clause attachment in L2 English
content.abstract: This paper analyses the effect that proficiency and reading experience, measured as weekly reading hours in English, may have on L2 English speakers’ relative clause attachment preferences. Thirty L2 English speakers with either Spanish or German as their L1 completed an online reading task where they were presented with thirty-two sentences containing relative clauses under two length conditions (long/short) and two position conditions (subject/object). An effect of proficiency or reading experience was expected to be found in their attachment biases following the Implicit Prosody Hypothesis
